source_caption: Long before street art was embraced by the mainstream, Downtown 81 captured New York City at its most unfiltered. Starring Jean-Michel Basquiat as himself, the film follows the young artist through the streets of early 1980s Manhattan, documenting a city fueled by graffiti, music, experimentation, and relentless creative energy. More than a portrait of Basquiat, it preserves a generation of artists transforming abandoned buildings, sidewalks, and subway cars into living canvases. At a time when creativity existed largely outside the traditional gallery system, the city became the artwork itself. Decades later, Downtown 81 remains a powerful time capsule of a cultural movement that forever changed the way we think about art, public space, and urban expression.

source_details.title: Downtown 81
source_details.synopsis: Downtown 81 is a 2000 American film shot in 1980–1981. The film was directed by Edo Bertoglio and written and produced by Glenn O'Brien and Patrick Montgomery, with post-production in 1999-2000 by Glenn O'Brien and Maripol. It is a rare real-life snapshot of an ultra-hip subculture of post-punk era Manhattan. Starring renowned artist Jean-Michel Basquiat and featuring such East Village artists as James Chance, Amos Poe, Walter Steding, Tav Falco and Elliott Murphy, the film is a bizarre elliptical urban fairy tale. In 1999, Michael Zilkha, founder of ZE Records (the label of several of the film's artists), became the film's executive producer.
